details.description: Cogito v1 preview (3B) is Deep Cogito's smallest hybrid reasoning model, an instruction-tuned checkpoint built on Meta's Llama-3.2-3B base and released April 8, 2025 as an open-weight preview under the Llama 3.2 Community License. It can respond directly like a standard chat model or switch into a self-reflective reasoning mode, trained using Deep Cogito's Iterated Distillation and Amplification (IDA) method rather than large-scale inference-time search. It supports a 128K-token context window and native tool calling, and is tuned for coding, STEM, instruction following and general helpfulness across more than 30 languages.
advantages: Supports a self-reflective 'thinking' reasoning mode in addition to standard direct-answer mode, activated via system prompt or tokenizer flag, per Deep Cogito's model card.
Supports single, parallel, multiple and parallel-multiple tool-calling configurations, per Deep Cogito's model card.
Trained in more than 30 languages, per Deep Cogito's model card.
disadvantages: This is a preview release (v1), not a stated general-availability version, per Deep Cogito's naming.
use_cases: Tool calling / function calling in agentic applications

notes: Catalog facts list max_input/output tokens as 131,072, matching Deep Cogito's stated 128K-token context window for this model. Deep Cogito's model card lists this checkpoint's parameter count as 4B despite being built on the 3B-parameter Llama-3.2-3B base. No numeric benchmark scores could be extracted from the model card or blog post beyond qualitative claims -- the underlying charts are images, so evaluations is left empty rather than guessed. Deep Cogito states the model has higher multilingual/coding/tool-calling capability than size-equivalent models but does not attach a number to that claim, so it was left out per the no-unattributed-superlatives rule.
